[h1]2,800+ Hours Here and Still Counting...[/h1]I'm not exaggerating when I say this is the best game ever made. Its pure perfection. It is F2P, has a [b]FREE[/b] battlepass, no paywalls, and no P2W content. Its all free. Even the premium currency (Platinum) is earnable through trading.Let alone the [b]HUMONGOUS[/b] amount of content we get every update. The variety is insane:[list][*] You can be a space ninja who obliterates everything.[*] You can mine gems, go fishing, or catch wildlife for preservation.[*] You can spend hours styling your look because Fashion Frame is the [i]true[/i] endgame.[*] You can breed doggos and mutant cats (Kubrows/Kavats).[*] You can captain your own massive battleship (Railjack).[*] You can play a Roguelite/Souls-like mode (Duviri).[*] You can create your own personal nemesis who mocks you until you hunt them down (Liches/Sisters).[*] You can pilot a giant ancient mech to stomp enemies into dust.[*] You can compose and play songs on the Shawzin.[ckflips on a hoverboard (K-Drive).[*] You can play "Ikeaframe" by decorating your Orbiter, Dojo, or basically anything.[*] You can literally go back to 1999 and date Aoi aka mag.[/list]Then there is the [b]Story and Lore[/b].It might start as a simple action game, but it evolves into a deep, dark, and emotional cinematic masterpiece that hits harder than most AAA single-player games. The lore is incredibly rich, spanning centuries of history, tragic characters, and plot twists that will leave you staring at your screen in silence. Quests like [i]The Second Dream[/i] and [i]The New War[/i] are absolute peak fictionand just like everything else, the entire story is 100% free.The amount of content you can explore and enjoy is amazing. I'd rate the game 10/10 but that doesn't seem fair to me.[h1]2,147,483,647 /

Definitely my favorite game! I love that the game is flexible enough to fit different playstyles of gamers from fast pace grind to more methodical story based driven gameplay...and everything in between. Gunplay is great and the movement is fluid (to say the least). Don't even get me started on the customization!All in all this game feels like a one stop shop. The biggest weakness is also this games greatest strength; there is SOO much to do and it can be overwhelming. The community is great and are always willing to help but, even that can be a bit much because of the sheer amount of content you will have to take in as a new player. I would recommend playing slow and probably solo for a bit when you're beginning the game so you can get a grasp of the gameplay and in game systems at your own pace. Google...and the loving community will still be there for you when you're ready.Lastly, did I mention almost everything in the game is free? There are literally a handfull of items that are exclusive to physical money purchases...but, for the most part you can Grind to get pretty much anything. Most of the in game Grinds are manageable, especially with groups or friends. In this game, there is plenty to do and plenty to grind for. However, if you do open you wallet, Digital Extremes definitely deserves it for this masterpiece! TLDR: The game is great if you give it a chance; take your time at first and don't try to do too much at once. Have fun!Good Luck Tenno!*Play on console with 1000+ hrs at time of post*

I'm not exactly sure what they're trying to do with this game, I've given it a shot multiple times over the years but so far I've not been able to determine any sort of endgame content or even any content that is remotely difficult. You spend almost all of your time running around killing everything you see in one hit, and sometimes even the enemies you can't see as well, farming materials to unlock characters and weapons. However, all of the story content for the game requires you to play as different characters with pre-determined abilities and weapons, meaning you essentially grind for... nothing? What's the point of unlocking warframes and new weapons and getting good mods for them when the content is not difficult and doesn't use anything you grinded for?This is basically half a game with a bunch of weird and conflicting nonsense. It was fun to play when I was quitting smoking and just needed to waste time but that's essentially all you're doing when you play this game, you're literally just wasting time. Just play it already, if you're reading reviews, it can't possibly do this game justice.To Preface this, I have around 600h now on PC but I mostly played on Xbox prior to about 4 months ago, so my playtime is probably around 2500h now or so? Been playing since Beta.STAY SPOILER FREE AND DON'T SPOIL IT FOR OTHERS!!!!Trust me, it's worth it! You're in this for the long haul, there is so much to do, just take it slow, have fun, progress the Star Chart (Navigation Console) and get used to the atmosphere, gameplay, and have fun. I'd recommend doing the bare minimum for the Open World sections until you've had "The Big Reveal"Don't buy anything at first, maybe colour pallets or cosmetics, but there is absolutely no need to pay real money for Warframes or Weapons as everything in game (besides most cosmetics) can be earned for free. It's also fairly easy to sell things you have to other players to get Platinum (premium currency)If you have a friend that plays, have them direct you and have them experience it with you (please, it feels so good to onboard new players and see their reactions), it also helps because this game can be quite confusing.If you need help with modding, I'd recommend searching "Brozime _____" on Youtube as IMO he does the best builds. He also does fresh account playthroughs somewhat regularly, which can be a decent guide for new players to get started.Please, just have fun with it. I'm not sure what to say about this game. It's free to play, has some microtransactions, asks you to wait while things build, but still respects your time. It has rotating timed events, that always come back. It's been running for 13 years and just recently put out an entirely new quest for tutorialization, complete with the attempt to match audio and some scriptwriting to how things were back when. I can't say much about the story, because it is spoilers and I do want you to experience it yourself. You are a Warframe, unless you're a Tenno. But you're also the Operator. Maybe things will make sense, maybe they won't, but when you wake up you have grineer to fight and an Earth to run around on. Yes, this Earth.The game starts you as a double-jumping bullet-hopping space ninja with magic powers, and you just get more and more of that, until you start clearing rooms with explosive powers or even more explosive weapons at the end-game. it's all a gradual progression. The game eases you into these new mechanics as best as its able, and when it fails, it has a fantastic self-run wiki and the community itself is mostly very nice. It has hundreds of weapons and 63 frigging Warframes at time of writing, so if you like the game at all its very very likely you'll find something that appeals to you - and quite possibly several, as I have. Maybe you'll like Valkyr, the berserker woman who screams real loud and gets real mad and then she does 300% melee damage and everything explodes. Maybe you'll enjoy Cyte-09, a consummate sniper who can throw out elemental damage ammo packs, turn invisible, and summon a sniper rifle out of thin air before headshotting 7 people with a richochet bullet. My personal favorite, if a bit basic, is Mag. She puts bubbles on people. The bubbles absorb things like enemies, and bullets, and projectiles, and sometimes magic birds, and mulch anything inside them. Then the bubbles explode. I love Mag.Please, play Warframe. At least try it. It is totally gods damn free. You don't have to put over 1000 hours into it like I have, but I can tell you I wish i did so first here rather than some other games of an outwardly similar nature.  It altered my brain chemistry. This story requires a bit of setup.Dealing 5 billion damage to a 100 health points enemy is crucial for the plot, trust meWelcome to Warframe. Play the same mission 231 times for the peepeepoopoo blueprint.Last year, a friend of mine whom I'd known from gaming for a long time contacted me and told me about this great new game that was in beta that he was backing as a founder (called a "Grandmaster" in-game) called Warframe. A third person cooperative shooter with elements of Phantasy Star Online/Diablo loot runs, procedurally generated levels, and more content being added all the time. The game was difficult to start, as there are many keys for various secret parkour maneuvers. Running along walls! Sliding down ziplines! Soon, I was completely hooked; my friend and I were playing late into the night, trying to grind out just one more piece necessary to build a new component or weapon, or trying to beat our best time on the Survival missions -- where you fend off an ever growing wave of foes as life support ticks down. Over the year, there were many great victories, hair raising last second escapes, and new friends joining our little group. Many hours were spent joking around with each other on Skype, cracking jokes, blasting weird songs at each other, and coming up with our own stupid little catchphrases.Flash forward a year; Warframe now has space combat, new Warframes, new weapons, and new combat controls. The game still has its original style, but it's so much improved. Last week, our four player regular team developed some incredible strategies that let us get further than we ever had on wave defense missions. The only thing that made us stop was getting tired.On Tuesday, my friend who invited me to the game a year ago didn't show up that night. I found out on Wednesday that he had passed away suddenly from an undiagnosed health condition. The shock of it is still hitting us hard. The friendships that we had formed through the game, gone in an instant. It hardly feels real. I keep expecting him to log in and be there, ready to do another defense mission, and it's difficult to accept that we'll be going it alone now.We contacted Digital Extremes, the company that makes the game, and asked if there was anything we could do. They dedicated their 11/20/2014 episode of their webcast to the memory of our friend and read our memorials to him on the air. Their reactions were heartfelt and touching. They really do listen to and react to the community.I not only recommend the game for how much fun it is (I recommend you play it with a group of friends on voice chat -- up to four per session; your gameplay experience may vary alone, and form a clan or join one just because many items are clan-only), I recommend it for how responsive the game developers are to the community. They constantly improve it and add new content, items, and weapons. There is a storyline that is unfolding. The voice acting is delightful. I love this game. It surprised me because it didn't seem like something i would enjoy, I'm not into guns or mechas.. But this game is so good, the movement feels amazing, the combat is smooth, the world building really interesting and the story is actually good! What else can i ask for?The huge variety of frames (or "classes") to choose from is great, it's almost guaranteed there is something you'll like and the best part is, all of them are good! You are not forced to play something you don't like just because its meta. Do whatever you want, make a good build and go for it! Only some are better to farm materials or do stealth quests, but that is all, in your normal gameplay loop, you will play whatever frame you enjoy. I can even play full melee or abilities only and never touch a gun! Now the part most would want to know.. Is this game reaaaally "free to play"? The answer is yes. You can use real money to speed up the crafting process, buy pre-built frames and weapons, or get exclusive cosmetics. But.. do you have to do any of this? The answer is no.Its totally up to you. You can just wait for the crafting process, you have a million things to do in this game meanwhile. You can get a bunch of other cosmetics for free just playing the game, and you can farm all the pieces to craft any frame or weapon you want. Also, you can play this game solo or in group (except some main quests that are solo), both feel good.As an extra: this game has some seriously good QoL that you dont see often. From small details like being able to choose between Hold/toggle for crouching or running, to change the color of your UI so your eyes don't hurt, or change easily the order of your A/B/C builds just by dragging them around.. It might not sound like a big deal, but it is, the game is comfortable to play and well designed.Another good thing is that it doesn't feel bad as a new player, i can catch up easily and the amount of content doesn't feel overwhelming, you have a lot to do but it doesn't make me feel like i have to do "everything" or i will be behind. I think its a very good game!

Warframe was thought to be a game about space ninjas. In many ways, it still is, but those words have begun to...change. For the better, that is. From intense combat to steady slice-of-life to romance sim to racing game to fighting game to pvp to pve to open-world to trading to fishing sim to extraction shooter to looter shooter to roguelike-A free game by the way.This game isn't something that should be swept under the rug. It's not intended to intimidate you, no, it wants to ease you in before hitting you with story that'll move you to tears. A game where time and community is at its very core. If you reach out, you'll notice a hand reaching back.I mean, seriously, this game can be intense with how many hours people have sunk into this game. However, I think the most clear sign of this game's life is that people still continue to play to this very second. The amount of replayability is honestly astounding.Together with a thriving community and developers who want to see this game succeed, this is a one of a kind thing. I mean, look at TennoGen. A cornerstone of the community that create unique customization options for the game, and instead of typical AAA corps sucking up all the money through labor of its fans, Digital Extremes decided to make it so those people get their money no matter what. Careers have been made from this, lives saved, and more talented artists continue to flock towards a friendly and accepting community. Did I mention that this game was free? Because it is.Yet...for all this time. For all the freedom we get. We are small.After all, it's the gaming world's best kept secret.Doesn't that...upset you, Tenno? To see a world, a universe that you've prospered in simply kept under wraps? Do you not wish to gain more? To fight together with the Lotus and to fend off all the opponents we may face? I want to start by saying that I genuinely enjoy grind heavy games, especially looter shooters, which are one of my favorite genres. However, this game takes grinding to an entirely different level. I understand why this is the case. It is a free to play title designed to eventually incentivize players to spend money to skip parts of the grind, but that does not make the experience more enjoyable.What makes the grind especially hard to justify is how easy the game is. I turned off matchmaking early on and completed the entire Star Chart solo, hoping that doing so would introduce some meaningful difficulty. Unfortunately, it never did. The game remains extremely easy from start to finish. I understand that Warframe is meant to be a power fantasy horde shooter, but with such a deep build system and a complex modding framework, you would expect at least a few enemies or encounters that truly test your builds.I have put a lot of hours into the game, and I am still waiting for that moment where an enemy actually forces me to question my setup or rethink my approach. That moment never came. Instead, the gameplay loop stays the same. You grind endlessly for more power, only to use that power to effortlessly wipe enemies. After a while, that becomes shallow and unrewarding.In hindsight, I probably should have stepped away much earlier, but I kept giving the game second chances, telling myself that the next planet or the next stage of progression would finally offer a real challenge. It never happened. From beginning to end, the game is a complete cakewalk.On a positive note, the movement system is excellent and the visuals are very impressive for a free to play game. Unfortunately, that is not enough to carry the experience. The excessive grind combined with the complete lack of meaningful difficulty makes the game feel hollow. At this time, I cannot recommend Warframe.

Current system is definitely a lot cleaner than it was, and the game as a whole has been polished time and time again, the only system that is still a headache is crafting.The good+Multiple attempts at Balancing in huge waves, makes it so certain weapons don't just become the only go-to 24/7+New mechanics as you progress, Incarnon's and Rivens, one gives a temp buff for a gun, other mods the gun and changes based on global player usage. I would comment about certain other parts but given they're spoilers, can't comment too much for the people who hadn't played yet. Get through 'The Second Dream', 'The War Within', and 'The New War' and you'll understand.+Options, there are lots of options for Ranged, Melee, Frames, Sentinels... If you don't pay attention to what's the best in slot, you'll rarely get the same loadout as another player. But there are some negatives about this which I'll bring up later.+Factions, we all appreciate the ability to gain reputations with certain factions... biggest ones being the Syndicates which are accessible relatively quickly upon getting in the game! Multiple options to take your pick, certain planets also having their own types of factions to rank up for stuff to do (which is another negative to make note of later).+Fast Early-game pacing, at first it'll be confusing how the hell people zip across the map the instant you launch a mission... it's really not too hard to get the handle of it, although I do understand the annoyance of wanting to take a certain speed in some missions, trust me it slows down *later*... and not for a good reason (which again, will be explained later).Now while a lot of that sounds good and there are other things I cannot come up with immediately, writing this while legit thinking of a reasonable list without making this a fucking novel... it should also note that this is just my opinion of what's good/bad, others may vary in opinion on this. So lets get to the negatives (you can agree or disagree, you do you).-Time Sinks, there is so fucking much of it... from Crafting to dailies, weeklies, time sensitive content (on planets), having to grind the bounties (because certain rewards are locked behind an RNG wall)... it's a nightmare trying to do this game casually without being time-gated in one way or another. Add in the recent [spoiler] 'Descendia' [/spoiler] which itself is another weekly thing to deal with along with Sorties, this game can become relatively close to a job with way too much to try and sift through.-RNG, Yes I am complaining about specifically the RNG in this game. Rivens I can understand as you are stat rolling... and it at one point had a means where people could spend money to reroll riven mods and had to remove it due to some 'over-spending' on it. My issue is more on the Bounties and VOID RELICS in this game and the actual chances of getting certain rewards. You can spend hours upon hours doing very specific void relics or bounties and not see a single rare out of hundreds of missions when the listed chance should be ~2-10%. I've had multiple times where I'll be in a run of full Radiants (10% chance for specifically the Rare), and all we'll see after 20 runs is just the common reward every time (Which at 50%, you'd expect the occasional Uncommon which is 40%). Given there is no means to guarantee a specific prime drop from a relic, or a means to get it without trading Platinum with another player, it really annoys the shit out of me that this is effectively gambling where some of these Relics can roll a Forma blueprint... which brings me to my next point.-Forma Blueprints suck, they can show up anywhere and everywhere and relics that have it are likely to specifically GIVE the Forma than anything else. I don't know if this is just me, but anytime I've rolled a relic with any % chance of a Forma Blueprint to show up, 3x chance anytime the relic is cracked open. If I am opening a Relic, I am specifically trying to get the Prime part from it, not the forma... and I am sure that others can agree that we need Forma's to be consolidated elsewhere over being a random grab bag reward that gets shoved everywhere.-Too much to grind for. You know how I mentioned there was a negative for Options? Where here it is. The game has way too much stuff to farm for, there is a reason this game has so many joke names from Bug-frame to Farm-frame. Each one takes its own time to grind for and then build... Warframes take 4 days (if you intentionally build it as quick as possible, 12 hours for each part and THREE FUCKING DAYS FOR THE WHOLE FRAME) and weapons take 12 hours each time. With over 100 frames (including primes) and over 600 FUCKING GUNS... you might want you take a look at your calculator, because not including the Founder exclusives and Kuva/Tenet/Coda weapons... ~109 warframes (primes included) -1(STARTING frame) another -1 (Umbra Excalibur), thats 321 DAYS for the Warframes alone not including the grind to even acquire the parts and building those first (worse with Prime Warframes via RNG or BUYING THE PARTS FROM OTHER PLAYERS). Weapons on the other hand is roughly 669 - 3 for the starting weapons you get another 333 days building all of those separately. Yeah, and that's just the build time for those things. It's impossible for me to calculate the time it'd take to actually get the parts, the materials for said parts, the blueprints for each and every thing in the game... the time to build a Dojo (unless you join someone else's which I would highly recommend to be able to access the blueprints from them)... Railjack, Duviri, literally all the content in the game to sift through for every single thing accessible. There is just way too much to go for if you want to 100% the game. I would strongly advise not making it your goal in this, you will lose your sanity.-This leads to another gripe of another type of Grind... Faction grinding through Bounties. Why is this a problem? Well, given how much time it takes to farm [b] MULTIPLE [/b] fucking factions of various kinds with the same gameplay loop you're probably used to, it can get mind numbing especially since there is a daily cap, cap increases based on your Mastery Level. Which goes up to a Maximum of 31,000 roughly at MR30. This is a problem for two reasons, you get people who want to rush these dailies so they can go onto other things, and you get people who are willing to AFK leech so they can leave their PC to do other things while other people do the hard work. The amount of times I've had to report people for being AFK in Fortuna and Plains of Eidolon... is just... fuck. If you ever encounter them, screenshot/video record and send it through https://support.warframe.com/hc/en-us/articles/200039839-Contacting-Customer-Service . The ingame report only really helps with chat related incidents, not gameplay related.Legit all I can fit in review, but theres more that I can comment about this stuff. Warframe is F2P, but it's also so heavy in content that it's going to be suffocating for new players. It's been around since 2013, lots of stuff since. While the grind is to be expected, having so many time-gates feels excessive and not player friendly... especially to casuals. Givin Negative because at this point you need a wiki to grind.

I'm writing this review because I keep getting asked by friends, if I want to play or why I stopped. This is now my shortcut review so I don't have to repeat myself. It's a Looter Shooter/Grinding Game (so know what you get into, it's not much skill but collecting things to build a more deadly warframe), it's fun to play with friends (essentially a hangout to talk and murder your way through the level) as you can in general play on your own pace and style (PvE) and the devs keep adding new things to the storyline, generally a healthy community (as always minor exceptions you should just ignore/block and report to keep things civil).I stopped playing in late 2024 due to the Lich mechanic and the initial grind you'd have to do (theoretically it will become "faster" after, at least in theory). So essentially you've to do some mission type over and over again to get relics. Then you do the next mission type over and over again to crack said relics to get a glyph. Then you hunt the Lich over and over to get the right glyph combination to finally kill them to get a weapon (or convert them to a crew member). Sure there are "strategies" but essentially it's a multi stage gambling to get the relics then to get the glyphs before any of the so called "strategies" to decipher the required combination.This grind was just too annoying for me in the end (considering you do this essentially alone because friends/other players stay out of it because it's too mind numbing. And no, now I do not want any help with this anymore, I asked before and won't waste any more time into this). The following tipped me over: Digital Extreme had the grand idea during this grind to even ask "Are you still enjoying the Game?". I put around 1700 hours into Warframe. I grinded everything, pushed through every wall, aimed for endgame, and genuinely loved it. Then suddenly  boom  Im permanently banned for a chat argument from months ago. Someone provoked me, insulted me, kept poking at me, and I finally reacted. One moment, one sentence  and apparently 1700 hours dont matter. For some people thats literally years of grind wiped out instantly.Heres the part people really need to understand  because I didnt, until it was too late:You dont need to be insulting someone.You dont need to mean anything malicious.You can literally be joking with your own friends.You can say something that wasnt intended to offend anyone at all.And guess what?A single moment, a single slip-up, one stupid sentence in clan chat or squad chat  and months later it can still come back and obliterate your entire account. No warning, no tlut temporary timeouts.They go straight for remove this player from existence.After my ban, I started digging into it  and it turns out this nonsense is everywhere. People get banned for harmless jokes, friendly sarcasm, or something taken completely out of context. Even long-term players with perfect histories get wiped instantly. The system doesnt care what you meant or who you were talking to  it just swings the hammer without thinking.And heres the part that really makes you laugh (or rage):Loyalty means absolutely NOTHING.1700 hours? Doesnt matter.3000 hours? Doesnt matter.5000 hours? Still doesnt matter.You can be the most dedicated, helpful, legitimate player ever  if you type one wrong word once, even if it wasnt serious, even if it was friendly banter, even if you were DEFENDING yourself, the system will nuke your account without hesitation. You might as well send your ticket to a refrigerator  at least it wont pretend it cares while giving you copy-paste nonsense.Lets be clear: rules are fine. But going straight to PERMANENT deletion over a dumb moment, a sarcastic joke, or a heated argument is ridiculous. Its like handing someone a life sentence for arguing in a supermarket. Humans joke. Humans argue. Humans get annoyed. Humans make mistakes. But in Warframe? Youre expected to be a flawless, emotionless robot 24/7.And the most ridiculous part?Chat is basically the backbone of the entire game.Trading, recruiting, clans, squads, help channels  without chat, Warframe would collapse. Stay eft with?The irony is painful.Honestly, once the shock faded, I almost felt relieved. Because the truth? The grind is brutal. Also, its hard to beat a free game with how much is in it.Since the change in leadership and their creative direction, the game is moving away from the high octane shooter looter that I feel many people play the game for. What have they added in recent updates? More fun and interesting content? More high adrenaline missions to farm for rare items? More story that explains the backstory of the star system you play in? No... a dating sim... Why a dating sim in a game about alien ninja war machines ripping through hordes of enemies? What a fantastic question. The Drifter is lame and this isn't why I play the game. Look at Nova, one of the oldest frames, then look at those heirloom skins again. or better yet, look at base Ember and then look at her heirloom skin. Warframe - a looter shooter where you play as a Space Ninja, speeding through missions with acrobatics, modded weapons and space magic. Made by Digital Extremes (DE), it has beautiful audio, cool art, and feels excellent to move around.It is Free-to-Play, and uniquely you can farm premium currency(Platinum) by trading farmable items with other players, so even premium items can be obtained without paying real money. You will be reading the Warframe Wiki a lot due to the sheer volume of information that may not be explained ingame. The community is generally helpful too - we all lift together after all.So why am I giving this game a thumbs down after so many hours of gameplay?[b][u]What were the problems?[/u][/b]If I'm to summarize the problems with Warframe, it would be the [u]constant need for escalation[/u], leading to:(1) [b]Powercreep[/b], which is [i]*very*[/i] poorly managed through [b]restrictions[/b],(2) [b]Unwillingness to fix old issues[/b] without a huge overhaul, but overhauls often aren't well-received because of:(3) [b]Overly rigid yet incoherent vision due to lack of playtesting[/b], resulting in many hotfixes to fix self-inflicted problems, which exacerbates:(4) [b]Community having stockholm syndrome[/b].Also don't say bad words in public chat, or you'll get banned. (Speaking with friends privately ingame is still okay)[b][u]My Profile:[/u][/b]I got into Warframe through a friend who is a long-time veteran player.The novelty of new gear, sense of progression, theorycrafting of builds, and my friend softening the worst aspects of the grind was what kept me playing.When I reached MR30 (now LR2), I expected a sense of achievement, but only felt emptiness. I looked back and realized I had wasted so much time on this endless grind to chase new shiny things. I also finally understand and see the game's many flaws, and the repetitive nature of how the game was handled in each new update.Ultimately, I've quit playing Warframe (as did my friend for other reasons), only hopping in when feeling nostalgic / curious to see what's new, and then log off immediately.[b][u]Elaborating on Restrictions:[/u][/b]The core idea of the game is that you are the Tenno, a master (collector) of all weapons. You refine your ability/knowledge on how to use those weapons to methodically take down hordes of ever-stronger enemies. Therein lies the problem.In order to keep escalating the gameplay, new tools get introduced to deal more damage, and the enemy level has to be increased to compensate. This results in an endless DPS race, old gear often be obsoleted, and defense objectives you have to protect eventually getting 1-shot by enemies.Instead of firmly re-scaling things back to ensure all loadouts are viable or allowing players to better select their preferred difficulty, [i]DE's approach is to continue inflating DPS (eg: Galvanized mods that increase damage as you kill more enemies with that specific weapon), and then turn around and artificially impose a forced DPS cap and various forms of gear/ability restrictions[/i]. Examples:[list][*]Damage Attenuation, so you can mow through mooks with 9 million damage and then suddenly only deal 100 damage to certain targets per hit.[*]Overguard as an additional layer of HP which prevents enemies from being affected by almost all crowd control, forcing you to build even more DPS.[*]Nullifying effects that outright disable your abilities(and usage of them) rather than simply no-sell it.[*]Only able to choose out of 4 randomly selected weapons that you may not like (including those you don't own), which may also be potentially too obsolete even with proper investment (while also giving a default configuration that is inferior to even minimal investment and can't meet the challenge).[/list]Beyond the DPS limitations, there's other forms of strange restrictions: Eidolon hunts and certain reward cycles require you to play at a very specific time of the day (eg: Rotation ABC for isolation vaults & bounties). Refusing to just give you innate loot pickup vacuum(which is otherwise a mandatory mod), or applying balance fixes to gear by giving augment mods(which is meant to serve as a modifier and not a addendum) and incarnon adapters rather than building the fix into the item innately. There's also been some strange decisions that have worsened QOL in the game, like reducing melee slam radius (understandable if misguided for nerfing slam builds, but makes breaking loot containers really annoying). Notice a trend here?It is clear that DE still envisions Warframe as a game where you methodically observe and take down enemies one by one at a certain slower pace (this philosophy is most clearly seen in the design of almost all the boss fights in Warframe). However, the reality is that Warframe rewards collecting the shiniest loot as efficiently and quickly as possible so that you can invest in your favourite gear to kill hordes in ever-faster and more creative ways, and DE is not able to reconcile this juxtaposition, resulting in many half-hearted measures that don't address or even worsen the root problem.Unfortunately, while the community is generally helpful, they would also often defend DE's decisions to their own detriment, attributing DE hotfixing their own self-inflicted messes as "listening to player feedback", which only encourages DE to keep doing the same song and dance. Dismissing/name-calling aside, the most common justification for these restrictions being that "You don't have to play this content, and can choose to play at a lower level to get the same reward slower"(except sometimes the reward requires playing the higher level) or play other content and trade for it. But that says more about the quality of the new content and defeats the purpose of playing in the first place, don't you think?[b][u]Closing:[/u][/b]The last few updates I've seen are also all pretty much the same - all one-off content islands based on the same old Bounty/Syndicate system that you don't want to do once you've finished farming for the new loot. Story-wise it is also pretty uninspired, and the focus had shifted away from Space Ninjas to the current focus on scripted "human" interactions with unlikeable characters. It is after considering all these factors that I've decided to leave the skinner box and go outside.At its core, Warframe is an enjoyable game, but be warned that once the novelty wears off and you see the endlessly repeating patterns, the disillusionment will hit you like a truck. Invest your time in Warframe at your own risk.

TL:DR - Warframe is a 12 year old game in a perpetual beta state that is wide as an ocean, but deep as a puddle. The game has been on a downtrend in quality for the past few years due to poor design decisions and a lack of overall direction.I cannot recommend Warframe as a long-time player due to the lack of an adequate in-game tutorials on the systems of this game. At its core, Warframe is an action RPG. This game requires that you do homework on the wiki to optimize your builds and understand the under-the-hood mechanics and calculations going on. The meat and potatoes of the game is building loadouts of different weapons, warframes, companions, and so on. This can only be comfortably reached when you have invested 250+ hours to complete the star chart (normal mode and hard mode), all quests, collected all the mods you need, 10+ systems with daily progression caps, and more. Due to bottlenecks related to the limited number of starter inventory slots, account level progression (mastery rank) is halted unless you pay for more slots with Warframe's premium currency, platinum (in-game trading or bought with IRL cash). If you are unwilling to pay, or don't have the platinum, you have to sell weapons/warframes to free up slots. Next you will have to sink hours into farming upgrade resources and the upgrades themselves, and then eventually you can actually get to the core of this game - build crafting & playing high-level content. If all this sounds familiar, this follows the "It gets better X hours in" cliche that is indicative of a game's bad pacing.Realistically there is no real endgame, just more "content islands" to farm in the archipelago that is Warframe. (No raid-style content, no active or fleshed-out PvP). The developers, Digital Extremes, rarely listen to actual feedback and they have an army of partnered content creators who are incentivized to worship the ground they walk on. If you do decide to play Warframe, expect updates that make the game unironically worse, which may include awful UI changes, unnecessary "reworks" to playable warframes, and oblivion-level jank.  Play at your own risk, Warframe does not respect your time.

Even after thousands of hours, youll still be stuck dealing with the same time gates - for Syndicates, Archon Shards, and especially for crafting basics like Formas and Adapters.The game isnt P2W, but it sure demands a lot (like, A LOT) of premium currency for basic things - inventory slots, weapon upgrades, FORMAS. Why does this player with 3000 hours not recommend this game that everyone seems to so highly praise?The answer isn't that simple as there are a multitude of reasons to why I would recommend absolutely not installing this absolute pointless game that has been permanently kept afloat by toxic positivity.Reason number 1: Bugs. every single damn update is an update littered with bugs that makes the game so unenjoyable, or reintroduces old bugs that makes the game so unplayable its not fun. Example: My favorite weapon a while ago (kuva zarr) had its reload mechanic bugged (this was similar for any weapon that had the same reload mechanism), it made the weapons completely not useable, and it didn't get fixed for months and months. When it comes to bugs if you don't get lucky and the bug isn't fixed within the first hotfix that gets released, well good luck it most likely will be in the game till the next major update which will be months and months later.Reason number 2:Remember at the beginning of my review were i stated the game is "pointless"? This game gaslights you into thinking it has mountains and mountains of meaningful content when it does NOT because no matter how much gear you get, no matter how much you invest into your kit there is NOTHING TO DO WITH  IT. THERE IS NO ENDGAME. so you have to do the same gamemodes over and over again, which on paper is fine, you can test different weapons and loadouts and min max to be efficient at getting rewards right? WRONG the game is completely not rewarding at all with absolutely no scaling in the rewards you get for completing harder levels of content. when the game refuses to respect your time, why should you play it?Reason number 3:Toxic positivity of the communityThis is what has done more damage to the game than anything else. No matter what the developers do to the game, there are a flock of losers who immedietly D ride Digital Extremes making up any excuse like "oh but the game is free" so any complaint you have is automatically invalidated. What an absolute joke. And when this toxic positivity exists to such a large extent NO FEEDBACK is taken unless 90% of the community complain about a certain thing.Reason number 4:They have completely removed any difficulty this game has to offer.Back in the day to play this game and reach high levels you actually had to try and get a full squad of people with synergies and certain methods of min maxing to be able to achieve the optimal result.Nowadays you don't need to have any sort of squad formation or any sort of effort at all to complete any content in this game, they've made it basically a close your eyes and anything will die. The enemies are simply too weak, and when they announced last year during their Jade Shadows update that they were updating the current armor and health system of all factions I was so excited for a refresher to the old system we had, only to introduce so many more flaws.Now every enemy is a piece of wet paper that you can kill with your eyes closed and no investment into your gear at all which is completely unsatisfying and unrewarding to me and anyone's effort of investing their time into the gameNow there are sooo many more issues that I can bring up including the recent horrendous optimization of the game as well as the lack of creativity with the re-use of the syndicate bounty system every update, but what finally got me to make this review was how horrendous the Vallis Undermined update was.It was absolutely INFESTED with bugs from core game mechanics like wall latching, to mods on weapons not working (nightwatch napalm), the new damage attenuation system that is introduced is also the most vile thing I've ever seen added to a game, the whole point of the rework was to make us be allowed to do more damage and feel the investment we put into our gear, what did we get? WE CANNOT ONE SHOT LEVEL 1 ENEMIES BECAUSE OF A CAP IN THE DAMAGE WE DO, nice damage attenuation fix. If you're going in solo, I'd say give this game a pass. The new player experience has gotten better in the 10 years since I last played, but it still has a long way to go. There's too much to learn, too little guidance, and too much filler.If you happen to have a veteran to help guide you and avoid the worst of the grind and all the traps, then the initial on-ramp isn't so bad. Warframe is the only F2P game I've come across that doesn't just feel like a diluted re-skin of a better game. Mechanics are sweet, loot isn't just about the numbers, and there's even some great story points. Still some work even if you pay, but more rewarding than many AAA games.
